title: Decompose burst surge, create autoscale runbook, and tune throttles to prevent GPU pool exhaustion
creator: Maya Chen
description: Follow-up work from the hosted API GPU exhaustion incident: break the observed burst behavior into reproducible components, formalize an autoscale + admission control runbook, and converge on throttle settings (per-tenant and per-route) that prevent queue amplification without overly degrading P50 latency. This ticket owns the investigation, k6/fuzz harnesses, runbook, and a small set of conservative server-side mitigations to ship in the next runtime patch.
acceptance_criteria: Repro harness that reliably triggers queue buildup in staging with configurable workload shapes (wide fanout, long-running batches, KV-cache-unfriendly prefixes)
Autoscale runbook committed to ops repo with playbook steps for priming, emergency scale-up, and safe scale-down
Per-tenant admission throttle defaults and a route-level fast-fail policy implemented behind a feature flag
End-to-end test that shows 50% reduction in tail queue lengths under synthetic surge compared to current baseline
Dashboard panels and alerts for the new token-level admission metrics and queue amplification indicator
reproduction_steps: Deploy a staging pool with the same kernel/profile mix as production (A100:32gb + cudnn kernels) and disable prefix cache to simulate cold cache conditions
Run the surge harness: 10k concurrent short requests followed by a 1k long-sequence burst across 200 tenants, with an 80/20 skew on top tenants
Observe queue length, admission scores, GPU utilization, per-request batching size, and KV cache miss rate for 30 minutes
Validate that backpressure signals are delayed (queue grows) and that autoscaler does not prime fast enough without priming triggers
action_items: (Arman) Build surge decomposition harness in tests/perf/surge-harness and add parameterization for seq len, tenant skew, and prefix-coldness — ETA 2025-02-28
(Maya) Draft autoscale runbook: priming thresholds, emergency scale commands, cost guardrails, and rollback procedure — ETA 2025-03-04
(Ravi) Implement conservative per-tenant admission throttle and fast-fail path behind FF: admit_score cap + token-per-second windowing — PR opened ENG-98079 — ETA 2025-03-11
(Priya) Add queue amplification metric (queued_tokens / active_tokens) and token-admission histogram to Grafana and link to incident dashboard — ETA 2025-03-07
(SRE) Implement a short-lived scale-prime lambda that can pre-warm pools when surge-detection alert triggers — prototype and runbook task ENG-98080 — ETA 2025-03-14
(QA) Add e2e test asserting P95 latency below SLA under admission policy with surge harness — ETA 2025-03-10
notes: 2025-02-18: Initial triage discovered two orthogonal causes: (1) rapid tenant-level request spikes causing large per-GPU queue amplification, and (2) autoscaler cooldown logic that prioritized cost stability over recovery speed.
2025-02-20: Decision: prioritize safe fast-fail admission and priming playbook over aggressive autoscale changes for immediate mitigation (PM and Infra review approved).
2025-02-24: Engineering review feedback: prefer token-window admission (sliding window) to per-request rate limits to avoid starving long-lived streaming sessions; added to action items.
2025-02-26: Prototype PR (internal): github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/5482 implementing admit_score cap. Perf results show 30% reduction in median queue length in local test.

2025-03-01: Observability note: existing GPU pool panels lacked token-level admission metrics; adding these revealed that admission signals were emitted but had poor SLI coverage — tied to ENG-98079 and observability tickets.
2025-03-03: PM asked to evaluate customer-visible fallbacks for high-value tenants; added as follow-up to determine whether VIP customers get sticky priming or grace credits.
Reviews: Security and compliance reviewed runbook steps for emergency scale operations; no keys or secrets exposed — security review not required for initial mitigations.
